 Ticketmaster Names Former Amazon Executive Jim Freeman CTO as It Expands AI Push
 Monday, 19 October 2026, 19:03 
 Photo source: Variety 
 Ticketmaster has appointed three senior executives and added the team from an AI startup it acquired in July as it expands its use of artificial intelligence. 
 Jim Freeman is Ticketmaster’s new chief technology officer, filling a role vacant since February. His predecessor, London-based CTO Carlos Alvarez-Coch, left ahead of a deposition in the U.S. government’s antitrust trial against Ticketmaster’s parent company, Live Nation.
 This is reported by Variety .
 The company also named Rachel Smith, a Block veteran whose former company owns music service Tidal, its first senior vice president of data science and machine learning. Chuck Mortimore, a product veteran of Disney and Stripe, will become senior vice president of product.
 Advertisement 
 Ticketmaster has also brought on the team from Raige.ai, an AI startup it acquired in July. The team will help expand the company’s use of AI tools and develop its AI infrastructure.
 “Reliable, secure and personalized experiences depend on how effectively we use technology and data,” Saumil Mehta, Ticketmaster’s global president, said in a statement. “Jim, Rachel, Chuck and the Ragie.ai team will help us move faster, build better tools and deliver better outcomes for fans, artists, venues and clients.” 
 – Saumil Mehta
 As CTO, Freeman will oversee AI tools, the use of the technology in fan experiences and its adoption across Ticketmaster. Before joining the company, he was a senior adviser at Permira. He previously served as a vice president at Amazon, where he worked on building and launching Prime Video and its device and distribution partnerships.
 Smith will focus on data science and analytics, including closer integration of data with Ticketmaster’s broader product development. Mortimore will help lead product strategy, including efforts to address bot issues and make it easier for fans to access their accounts and tickets.
 See also: 
 The civil antitrust trial against Live Nation will resume after state attorneys rejected a proposed DOJ settlement; witnesses including CEO Michael Rapino and Kid Rock are expected to testify. 
 Mistral has introduced ML4, an open-weight AI model the French company says can rival leading closed systems. The model’s performance claims have not been independently verified.
